known_issues.title: Provider shown as in-network for the patient's plan is not
known_issues.what: Patient enters their plan, searches, picks a provider badged in-network and books. The office then calls or the claim comes back to say the provider does not accept that plan (or that specific plan variant). Many patients only learn this at the visit or when a bill arrives, so they lose the visit, pay out of pocket, or rebook. Several say it happened on multiple bookings. A recurring sub-pattern is providers who book through a third-party practice network listed as accepting plans they don't. Another is specific plan variants (state/public plans) being lumped into a broader carrier entry.

story.headline: Wrong in-network badges, phantom open times: 7 of 12 lost a visit, trip or money.
story.lede: We read all 64 September tickets: 39 were real reports and 12 patients said they lost a visit, trip or money. Seven of those 12 trace to two problems: wrong in-network badges and open times the practice could not keep. The biggest complaint was AI search: 6 patients asked to turn it off.

patterns.title: Provider badged in-network for the patient's plan turned out not to be
patterns.confidence_reason: MEDIUM rule: 4 confirmed tickets describe the same failure (badge said in-network, practice or claim said otherwise). Not the top level: under 5 confirmed, and none of September's tickets link to a tracking item.
patterns.impact: All 4 said they lost a visit, trip or money: cancelled visits, rebooking more than once, or a bill after the visit.
patterns.patients_report: They entered or uploaded their plan, booked a provider marked in-network, then the practice cancelled or the claim came back out-of-network. Some hit it with several providers in a row.
patterns.history: This pattern was seen in every month of the window and peaked in June at 10. September's 4 is near its usual level, which does not mean it is getting better.
patterns.team_knows: Support confirms the listing showed in-network when booked and routes the patient on. Two action items on team boards are still To Do; none of September's tickets link to them.
patterns.likely_cause: Practices keep their own accepted-plan data and it is out of date or too broad. Specific plan variants get filed under a general carrier entry.
patterns.pm_action: Insurance (provider network data): take a month of bookings badged in-network that were later cancelled for an insurance reason, re-check each provider's accepted plans with the carrier directory, and measure the mismatch rate by plan variant. Confirmed if mismatches cluster in specific plan mappings; refuted if the listed data matches the carrier.
